business_problem: Audacy needed to replace messy point-to-point integrations and inconsistent schemas so it could personalize content, support dynamic advertising, and engage listeners in real time across audio platforms.
solution_summary: Audacy adopted Confluent's cloud-native data streaming platform to build a real-time data backbone for its audio streaming, podcast, and broadcast businesses. The new architecture replaces point-to-point integrations with shared event flows so audience, metadata, and product signals can move across systems without custom rewiring every time a team adds a feature. Schema Registry standardizes those streams across microservices and data stores, while fully managed connectors integrate existing tools and destinations without burdening developers with custom integration code. Audacy uses that backbone to power listener-facing experiences such as Tap to Record, near-real-time screen and metadata updates, show alerts, and lower-latency live streaming. The platform also gives the company a better base for personalized content, advertising, and future stream processing closer to the source of data.

solution_components.role: Provides the shared real-time backbone for listener, metadata, and product events.

data_flow: Audience interactions, content metadata, and product events stream through Confluent, where standardized schemas and managed connectors make the data available to apps and downstream systems that update screens, trigger alerts, support interactive features, and optimize advertising in near real time.
business_outcome: Audacy accelerated feature delivery, improved listener engagement, lowered audio and metadata latency, and created a stronger base for data-driven advertising and partnerships.
